# Interface stability

Profile `core-v1` is **candidate** at Core API generation **1**.
This classification says which public interfaces are stable enough to treat as the beta contract, and which stay explicitly unstable.
It does not promote the profile and it does not change runtime behavior.

## What "core" means

Three existing uses of the word are not the same contract:

- **Beta contract.** The product allow-list in `profiles/core-v1.json`: the abstract symbols below, their per-binding names, the declared execution flavors, the reactive-graph fixture closure, and the installed-consumer scenarios.
- **Collection method list.** [Cell model § Core surface vs. binding extensions](../cell-model.md#core-surface-vs-binding-extensions) names methods a collection implementation must expose. That is a module conformance list. It is not this beta contract.
- **Rust facade.** `lazily::core` re-exports the allow-listed Rust names and also re-exports names that are not allow-listed. Always-compiled Rust modules are a build fact, not a promise.

## Beta contract

Only these abstract symbols are the beta contract.
A public name is in the contract only when that binding's `symbol_mappings` lists it.
A conformance fixture, a binding-matrix MUST, or a type that merely implements a flavor is not enough.

| Symbol | Kind |
| --- | --- |
| `context` | type |
| `source` | type |
| `computed` | type |
| `effect` | type |
| `batch` | operation |
| `scope` | operation |
| `typed_context` | type |

Execution flavors, for every candidate binding: `single_threaded`, `thread_safe`, `async`.
Flavor behavior is in the contract because those bindings must keep passing the reactive-graph closure on each flavor they declare.
The extra Rust type names that implement `thread_safe` and `async` are not in the Rust symbol mapping, so those names stay unstable.

Fixture closure: **18** `reactive-graph/` files; digest `sha256-path-nul-bytes-v1:7fe79ff9c316910903229437e0d57befe935d60c058c10fb43929b0ac3189fb7`.
Installed-consumer scenarios: `source-computed-effect`, `batch-coalescing`, `scoped-disposal`, `typed-context`.

Core remains pre-1.0, but a released Core symbol is kept compatible throughout its declared deprecation window; accidental breaks are defects.
A deprecated core symbol remains compatible for at least 2 compatible cohorts and 90 days.
Exports outside the declared Core allow-list remain Preview. Their presence in an umbrella package does not grant Core compatibility or Beta status.

## Explicitly unstable modules

Every profile module that is not `core` stays unstable.
An umbrella export does not promote it.

| Module | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| `collections` | Keyed maps, queues, topics, reconcile, and merge algebra. The collection-family method list in cell-model.md is a conformance requirement for that module, not the product beta contract. Its coverage family is excluded from core rows. |
| `statecharts` | StateChart and StateMachine are always compiled in Rust, and the statechart Cargo feature is a deprecated empty alias. Always-on compilation is not the product profile: statecharts stay a module, and the statechart coverage family is excluded from core rows. |
| `synchronization` | No abstract symbol and no core coverage row. Membership, leases, and coordination stay outside the beta contract. |
| `durable` | Durable owner, outbox, sinks, and sqlite, postgres, and JetStream hosts are specified and excluded from core coverage. A store conformance pin is not a beta API freeze. |
| `distributed` | CRDT plane, text and sequence CRDTs, and the lossless tree. The Rust lossless-tree feature stays off by default until that protocol stabilizes. Distributed coverage families are excluded from core rows. |
| `transport` | IPC, ingress, egress, WebRTC, websocket, signaling, and zero-copy transport. protocol_version 1 is conformance-locked and still additive. The binding matrix can require a layer without promising it will not change. |
| `codecs` | JSON, MessagePack, Postcard, and Protobuf follow the wire. They are not the reactive kernel and are excluded from the core allow-list. |
| `ffi` | The C-ABI claim is fixtureless and module-scoped. Shipping it in an umbrella package does not put it in Core. |
| `react` | Adapter. It may depend on the beta contract. The beta contract must not depend on it. |
| `r3` | Adapter with the same boundary as react. Not a candidate binding and not a beta contract. |

Capability exclusions are unstable by reference to the profile, not by a second list:
coverage families `materialization`, `familysync`, `statechart`, `collections`, `queue`, `topic`, `work-queue`, `crdt`, `lossless-tree`, `egress`, `ingress`, `codec`, `transport`, `message-passing`, `reliable-sync`, `durable-owner`, `durable-capability`, `distributed`, `receipts`, `security`, `membership`, `coordination`, `presence`, `temporal`, `rateshape`, `windowing`, `resilience`, `stdlib`, `service`, `instrumentation`;
public symbols `SourceMap`, `ComputedMap`, `StateChart`, `QueueCell`, `TopicCell`, `WorkQueueCell`, `TextCrdt`, `RelayCell`, `IngressCell`, `EgressCore`, `TimerCell`, `IpcMessage`, `ShmBlobArena`, `MergePolicy`, `ReactAdapter`, `R3Adapters`.

## Rust `lazily::core` facade

Allow-listed re-exports, cfg-free:
`Computed`, `Context`, `Effect`, `Source`, `TeardownScope`, `TypedContext`.

Unstable re-exports:

| Name | cfg | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Compute` | — | Tracked-read witness passed into a compute closure. Public from lazily::core, and not an allow-listed Rust name. |
| `ComputeOps` | — | Intra-model read trait implemented by Context and Compute. Not an allow-listed Rust name. |
| `AsyncComputed` | `async` | Async flavor handle. Declared flavors must keep passing the reactive-graph closure. This type name is not allow-listed. |
| `AsyncContext` | `async` | Async flavor context. Same split as AsyncComputed: flavor behavior is in the closure, the Rust name is not. |
| `AsyncEffectHandle` | `async` | Async effect handle. Not an allow-listed Rust name. |
| `AsyncSource` | `async` | Async source handle. Not an allow-listed Rust name. |
| `AsyncTeardownScope` | `async` | Async teardown scope. Not an allow-listed Rust name. |
| `ThreadSafeContext` | `thread-safe` | Thread-safe flavor context. The flavor is required evidence. The type name is not in the Rust symbol mapping. |
| `ThreadSafeTeardownScope` | `thread-safe` | Thread-safe teardown scope. Not an allow-listed Rust name. |
| `TypedThreadSafeContext` | `thread-safe` | Thread-safe typed context. Not an allow-listed Rust name. The allow-listed typed name is TypedContext. |

## Keeping the beta contract stable

- Keep profile status at candidate until an explicit promotion. This classification does not promote it.
- A beta-contract edit changes profiles/core-v1.json, the fixture digest, and this registry together. The checkers reject a one-sided edit.
- A released core symbol stays compatible for the deprecation window in the artifact-consumer policy: at least two compatible cohorts and 90 days. Removal needs deprecated_since, replacement, and earliest_removal on the symbol.
- Do not treat a MUST in the binding matrix, a conformance fixture, or an always-compiled Rust module as a beta promise. Those are implementation or module contracts.
- Widening the Rust allow-list to Compute, ComputeOps, or the async and thread-safe facade names would expand the promise. Leave them unstable unless that edit is intentional.
- Per-binding API snapshots and native diff gates are still future work. This lock is the allow-list, the fixture closure, the consumer scenarios, and the Rust lazily::core re-export split.

Per-binding names and imports stay in [Core Beta profile](core-beta.md).
Support ranges and the deprecation window stay in [Core support](core-support.md).
